page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing a total of 16 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The hypervisor layer is managed via KVM.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities alongside weak single-core execution. The single-core performance is rated as weak to poor, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 893.0 and a low single-threaded gzip compression rate of 19.01 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded operations perform at an average tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 13025.11 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 11776.53. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 75.3 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 53.85 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge lies in its high memory density relative to its compute power. While the 128.0 GB RAM capacity supports memory-intensive applications, the weak single-core performance limits its utility for sequential processing tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this hardware profile is optimized for workloads that require substantial memory capacity without demanding high-frequency CPU performance. It is suited for database operations, multi-threaded text and image processing, static web serving, and small-scale language model inference, where parallel execution can offset the lower single-core speeds.
